blocks.text: **One tag, one job.** Everything in these boxes is a tag with an NFC sticker inside. Tap it with a phone and it does one thing: gets your family’s number ready to call, shares your contact, joins the Wi-Fi. Here are the eight jobs in our boxes, what each does on an iPhone and on Android, and how to make your own.

items.text: **The sticker does the work.** A tap opens whatever was written to it. The other phone doesn’t need an app.
**Any phone with NFC.** Many Android phones have NFC off until you turn it on, and older iPhones (7 to X) need the NFC reader in Control Center.

**You write it.** Tilde for Android writes any of these in a few taps, for free: Cards → **Write a sticker**, then choose what it opens. `[depends on 1.3.0]` On an iPhone, the free NFC Tools app writes a link.

**You can rewrite it.** A phone rewrites the sticker through the plastic, so a tag can change jobs. `[depends on U15]` If Tilde protected the sticker, only the phone that wrote it can change it. `[depends on T-S1, T-S2]`
**Anything on a tag is public.** Anyone who taps it can read it and copy what’s on it. Put on it only what you’d put on a poster.

blocks.text: **The code on our tags:** some of the booth’s tags have a QR code on the front. It opens Tilde’s page (`taptilde.com`), not what’s on your sticker. `[depends on T-B1]` A tag you print yourself carries your own link in its code.
the two giveaway boxes, open: four stacks each
**If your child loses their phone, whoever finds them taps the tag on their backpack, and your number is ready to call.**

items.text: **Android:** a tap opens the phone app with your number filled in, ready to call. No internet needed. `[depends on T-N4, T-B6]`
**iPhone:** a tap shows a notification to call your number. `[depends on T-N2, T-B6]`
sub: If T-N2 fails, say: “iPhones can’t call from this tag yet: it’s for Android phones.”

items.text: **Make one:** in Tilde’s Cards tab, tap **+** (New card), then **Start from a template → Family → Create**. It’s named “Call my family” and shares your number, ready to call. Then use **Write a sticker**. `[depends on templates]`
**Keep in mind:** one parent’s number is enough. Don’t put on it the child’s name, school or address, or your own address: anyone who finds it can read it.

blocks.text: **Share your contact with any iPhone or Android phone: tap the tag, save the contact.**

items.text: **Android:** a tap offers to save your contact card, if it fits the sticker. A full card that doesn’t fit is written as its contact link, which opens your contact page with **Save contact** and needs internet. `[depends on T-B2]`; `[depends on 1.3.0, T1–T4]` for the contact link.
**iPhone:** a tap opens a page with your card and **Save contact**. It needs internet; your details travel in the link, after the #, and never reach a server. `[depends on T1–T4, T-B2]`
sub: If T1–T4 or T-B2 fail, the iPhone line goes, and the lead becomes “Tap the tag, save the contact” (Android).

items.text: **Make one:** **Write a sticker → Contact card**. Before you tap, Tilde says which sticker sizes fit your full card (a card with several links needs an NTAG216), and asks first if yours doesn’t. `[depends on T-W1–T-W7]`
**Keep in mind:** anyone who taps it gets your contact card. In Edit card, uncheck your phone number or email under **What they save** if you’d rather leave them off. `[depends on 1.3.0]`

blocks.text: **A tap opens your website, your LinkedIn or any page.**

items.text: **Android and iPhone:** a tap opens the link. No typing a URL.
**Make one:** add the link to a card on the Cards tab, then **Write a sticker** and choose it. On an iPhone, write it with NFC Tools.
**Keep in mind:** use it for yourself too, as a physical bookmark for a page you open every day (see below).

blocks.text: **A tap opens a WhatsApp chat with you, with a greeting ready to send. No more “text me your number”.**

items.text: **Android and iPhone:** a tap opens WhatsApp on a chat with you, the greeting filled in. `[depends on T-B3]`
**Make one:** add **WhatsApp** to a card, then **Write a sticker → WhatsApp**.
**Keep in mind:** the link carries your number, so anyone who taps it can message you.

blocks.text: **Friends over? They tap the tag and they’re online. No asking for the password, no typing.**

items.text: **Android:** a tap offers to connect to your network, and joins.
**iPhone:** a tap opens a page with the network’s name, the password to copy, and a code to show a friend. The page needs internet. `[depends on T-WF1–T-WF4]`
sub: If T-WF fails, say: “iPhones can’t join from a tag: they scan the Wi-Fi code on your phone’s Share screen.”

items.text: **Make one:** set up **Guest Wi-Fi** in Tilde’s Settings, then **Write a sticker → Guest Wi-Fi** (it’s named **Wi-Fi** if you’ve set up Hotspot too). With a long network name and password, the iPhone page needs an NTAG215 or 216 sticker, and Tilde says so before you write. `[depends on T-WF]` for the sticker size.
**Keep in mind:** use your guest network, never your main one. Anyone with the tag can read the password.

blocks.text: **One tap and your number is ready to call, or a new text to you, without saving a contact.**

items.text: **Android:** a tap opens the dialer with your number filled in (Call), or a new text to you (Text). `[depends on T-N3, T-N4]`
**iPhone:** a tap shows a notification to call you or text you. `[depends on T-N1, T-N2, per mode]`
sub: If T-N2 fails for a mode, say for that mode: “iPhones scan the code on your phone’s screen instead.”

items.text: **Make one:** **Write a sticker → Phone number**, then pick **Text** or **Call**. `[depends on T-N1–T-N7]`
**Keep in mind:** the text starts empty, and Call only fills in the number: nobody’s phone calls you by itself.

blocks.text: **Found this? Tap to call the owner.** For your keys or your bag.

items.text: **Android:** a tap opens the phone app with your number filled in, ready to call. `[depends on T-N4, T-B6]`
**iPhone:** a tap shows a notification to call your number. `[depends on T-N2, T-B6]`
sub: If T-N2 fails, say: “iPhones can’t call from this tag yet: it’s for Android phones.”

items.text: **Make one:** in Tilde’s Cards tab, tap **+** (New card), then **Start from a template → Lost & found → Create**. Its line is “Found this? Call or text me”, and it shares your number, ready to call. Then **Write a sticker**. `[depends on templates]`
**Keep in mind:** never an address. Keys plus an address is a way in. A first name helps whoever finds it.
**Android and iPhone:** a tap opens your booking page (Calendly, Google Calendar’s booking pages or any other). `[depends on T-B5]`
**Make one:** add your booking link to a card, then **Write a sticker** and choose it.
**Keep in mind:** use a booking page that shows only your free times, never your calendar’s details.

blocks.text: **Flip to the tag, tap, and it’s open.** A ring of thin tags works like index cards, each for a page you’d otherwise dig for: the parcel you’re tracking, today’s forecast, your gym’s schedule. These are for you rather than to share. Your phone rewrites a tag when the parcel changes, without a reprint. `[depends on U15]`
**The demo keychain:** flip through and tap any. At the booth, its tags open things like these:

items.text: a parcel’s tracking page;

blocks.text: A tracking page can show your name and address on some carriers’ sites, so keep those bookmarks on your own keys.
You don’t need a tag at all: Tilde shares from your phone with a tap or a code.

items.text: **Keep a card for every room:** a work card with your title and LinkedIn, and a socials card without your number.
**Remember who you met:** Met lists every tap of your phone, with the time, the card and the event. Add a note, then go through it after the event.
**At our booth:** take a tag from the boxes. We’ll write it for you, or show you how to write it with Tilde.
**Print your own:** coins and tags on the Tilde Keyrings listing (MAKERWORLD-KEYRINGS-URL). `[depends on keyrings listing]`
**Or any NFC sticker:** Tilde writes the same things to a plain round NFC sticker, or to a Tilde Card.
